title: Probe-type low water cut-off (Guard Dog RB-122E / FPC-1000): will not operate
equipment: McDonnell & Miller Guard Dog RB-122E and FPC-1000 probe controls

n1.text: Which control, and what is the LED doing? Ask the tech to read the LEDs.

g1.text: Does the RB-122E green LED blink 13 times, or 1 to 10 times, and the boiler will not start?

options.label: No blinking, control just fails to operate

r_g13.cause: The probe is shorting at power on.
fix: Turn off the boiler and check the probe wiring connection.
Turn off the boiler, drain it and remove the control to see whether the probe tip touches a metal surface.
Press the test button for more than 1 second until the red LED turns off, or power cycle to reset.
If it continues, replace the control.

g2.text: Ask the tech to measure voltage at wires H and N of the probe control. Is voltage present?

r_gnov.cause: No voltage is reaching the probe control.
fix: Make the necessary electrical corrections; check wiring against the installation steps.
If wiring is right and the problem remains, replace the probe control.

r_gprobe.cause: The probe may be touching the boiler or pipe wall, wrapped in PTFE tape, or sitting in an air pocket.
fix: Check there is a 2 inch minimum width in the boiler section or 1-1/4 inch pipe inner diameter around the probe.
Remove any PTFE tape and use pipe sealing compound on the threads.
Purge air around the probe by opening the water feed valve until water flows from the tapping.
Also look for other wiring or operating control problems.

f1.text: Does the FPC-1000 Green/Yellow LED blink 13 times, or 1 to 10 times, and the boiler will not start?

options.label: No blinking, probe fails to operate

r_f13.cause: The probe is shorting at power on.
fix: Turn off the boiler and check the probe wiring connection.
Turn off the boiler, drain it and remove the control to see whether the probe tip touches a metal surface.
Press the Test/Reset button for more than 1 second until the red LED turns off, or power cycle.
If the problem continues, replace the control.
Check the boiler water level is at or above the probe.
Recheck wiring against the boiler manufacturer diagrams or the manual.
Check that PTFE tape was not used on the electrode threads.
Some foaming is common in certain boilers; follow the boiler manufacturer cleaning recommendations.
